sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Gondwana Origin**: The peninsula is a part of the ancient Gondwana landmass, marked by a broad and shallow trough with a general elevation from west to east.
• **Relief Features**: Features relict mountains, faulted sedimentary basins, and vast undulating tablelands shaped by extensive **volcanic activity (Deccan Traps)**.
• **Delhi-Haridwar Ridge**: Connects the Peninsular block to the Himalayan region underneath the Indo-Gangetic Alluvial plain.
• **Key Metric / Factor**: Bounded by the Aravallis in the northwest, the Rajmahal Hills in the east, the Gir range in the west, and the Cardamom Hills in the south.

sections.title: Comprehensive Classification & Comparative Matrix
rows: Triangular landmass south of Narmada river; composed of basaltic lava flows (Deccan Traps); rich in black soil (Regur).
Cretaceous-Eocene period fissure volcanic eruptions linked to the Reunion Hotspot.
Frequent Prelims questions on soil types, river watersheds, and basaltic topography.
North of Narmada river, bounded by Aravallis on west and Vindhyas on south; drains into Ganga-Yamuna systems (Chambal, Betwa).
Upliftment of ancient mountain roots, extensive denudation, and river incision.
Source of north-flowing rivers and historic trade routes.
Meghalaya plateau and Karbi Anglong plateau; separated from main peninsula by the Malda Fault (Garo-Rajmahal Gap).
Subsidence of intervening land mass followed by sedimentation of Ganga-Brahmaputra.
Prelims trap: Often mistaken as part of the Himalayas due to high rainfall and Khasi/Jaintia hills.

items.definition: Massive expanses of volcanic rock formed by flood basalt flows covering large parts of western and central India during the late Cretaceous period.
A structural fault zone in West Bengal that separates the Meghalaya and Karbi Anglong plateaus from the main block of the Indian Peninsular Plateau.
A crescent-shaped sedimentary basin within the Dharwar craton of the Peninsular Plateau, highly rich in non-ferrous minerals and ancient quartzites.
Archean (Dharwar rocks), Proterozoic (Cuddapah and Vindhyan systems), and Mesozoic-Cenozoic (Deccan Traps).

items.title: Major Geographical Distribution / Regional Hubs
items.content:
• **Sub-Plateaus**: Malwa Plateau, Chota Nagpur Plateau, Bundelkhand, Baghelkhand, and Telangana Plateau.
• **Driving Advantages**: Mineral concentration (Chota Nagpur as the 'Ruhr of India'), hydroelectric potential, and fertile regur soil for cotton cultivation.

items.title: Challenges, Reforms & Forward Strategy
items.content:
• **Bottlenecks / Issues**: Soil erosion, unscientific mining leading to ecological degradation, water scarcity in rain-shadow zones of Karnataka and Maharashtra.
• **Policy Interventions**: Watershed management programs, District Mineral Foundations (DMF) under MMDR Act, and sustainable plateau afforestation.

items.title: Mnemonic for Central Highlands & Plateaus (North to South/West to East)
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym / Phrase**: 'Always Buy Fresh Choclates' (Aravalli, Bundelkhand, Malwa, Chota Nagpur - general regional sequence context).
• **Decoded Meaning**: Links major plateau zones from west to east.
• **Prelims Exam Value**: Instantly answers map-based sequencing questions.

items.title: Retention Rule of Thumb
items.content: • **Core Formula / Rule**: Rivers on the Peninsula flow West to East (Narmada & Tapti are the notable exceptions flowing East to West through rift valleys).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC frequently states that the Meghalaya Plateau and Karbi Anglong Plateau were formed as a part of the Himalayan orogeny. This is false; they are detached extensions of the Peninsular Plateau separated by the Malda Fault.
Mains Value Addition: In GS-1, analyze the Peninsular Plateau not just as a static landform, but as a dynamic mineral storehouse that drives India's heavy industry and energy security corridors.

keyTakeaways: The Peninsular Plateau is the oldest stable block of India derived from the Gondwana landmass.
It is broadly divided into the Central Highlands, Deccan Plateau, and the North-Eastern Plateau (Meghalaya/Karbi Anglong).
Except for Narmada and Tapti which flow through rift valleys into the Arabian Sea, the overall slope of the plateau is from west to east.
